title: Measure what each review layer catches: reviewer, refuter, fix verifier and design reviewer scored against past incidents
why: Owner, 19:45 CST Nov 17 (relayed by the consultant): review the Claude Code team blogs https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-code-team-thinks-about-verification/ and https://claude.dev/blog/solving-code-review-at-anthropic/ and land their findings. Triage read both through a page summary, not word for word. Finding: Verification blog: score reviewers against past incidents with one-sentence answer keys and merged changes as controls; measure raw, post-verification and final recall separately. Code-review blog: past incidents become an eval set that scores every reviewer change; one tuned primary reviewer beats stacking a second expensive one.
source: owner words 19:45 CST Nov 17 via the consultant; blogs read through a page summary
note: Harm if missing: we stack four review layers with no measure of what each catches, so a layer that adds cost and no catches stays. Brief: test-author first writes the eval fixture (incident list from reverts and red-main reverts, answer keys, merged controls) red on main; builder then makes the scorer run; report per-layer recall and cost. Proof command: the scorer's own run through `verdict`, plus the report file. Home to use: decision pr-review-record. Not built; no overlap found by grep of roadmap steps.
ask:

Governing: decision pr-review-record, roles-review-cap-three. Harm: four layers stack with no measure of what each catches.
1. test-author first (own worktree): write the eval fixture in the repo's test folder: incident list from reverts and red-main reverts (read from git and REST), an answer key per incident, and merged controls (PRs that merged clean). Show it red on main.
2. builder: make the scorer run and report per-layer recall and cost, with n.
3. reviewer (model per agent-model-cap).
